## Strict Stationarity

A time series $\{x_t\}$ is **strictly stationary** if the joint distribution of  
$(x_{t_1}, \dots, x_{t_k})$ is the same as  
$(x_{t_1+h}, \dots, x_{t_k+h})$ for all shifts $h$.

## Weak Stationarity

More commonly used. Requires:

- Constant mean: $\mathbb{E}[x_t] = \mu$
- Covariance depends only on lag:


$$\gamma(h) = \text{Cov}(x_{t+h}, x_t)$$

:::callout-tip
In this course, “stationary” usually means **weakly stationary**.
:::

## Examples

- White noise ✔
- Moving average ✔
- Random walk ✘
